NVIDIA L40S is the NVIDIA H100 AI Alternative with a Big Benefit
By Patrick Kennedy -October 31, 20231
NVIDIA H100 or L40S in Supermicro SYS-521GE-TNRT Servers
Something very different with today‚Äôs systems is that they are now a full 5U. This is generally because the TDP of each GPU, H100 or L40S is 350W. Commonly, these systems have eight GPUs for around 2.8kW in the GPUs. The other reason is that between the two options, these systems are typically using power in the 4.3-5kW range. That makes them enough for a single server per 208V 30A rack or several servers in a higher-power rack. Density is less challenging with modern AI servers since often power and cooling in racks is the bigger limiter.

Supermicro SYS 521GE TNRT 7
Supermicro SYS 521GE TNRT 7
That extra 1U of space allows for more cooling to the GPUs. NVIDIA GPUs and the H100 and L40S follow this lead and typically can use their maximum rated power, but they also usually use less than their rated power on average.

Supermicro SYS 521GE TNRT 39
Supermicro SYS 521GE TNRT 39
Supermicro has both Intel Xeon and AMD EPYC versions of the chassis. We had two Intel Xeon versions set up, one with 8x NVIDIA H100 GPUs.

Supermicro SYS 521GE TNRT 117
Supermicro SYS 521GE TNRT 117
And the other with the NVIDIA L40S cards.

Supermicro SYS 521GE TNRT 118
Supermicro SYS 521GE TNRT 118
You can see that these are set up with only eight cards, but these systems can scale up to 10, as we used in DeepLearning11 way back in the day.

Supermicro SYS 521GE TNRT 96
Supermicro SYS 521GE TNRT 96
With PCIe GPU servers, how GPUs are connected is important for things like P2P across a PCIe switch without NVLink, and how well NVIDIA NCCL works on the workload. NCCL is important to scale out jobs to multiple GPUs. The Supermicro SYS-521GE-TNRT uses PCIe Gen5 switches in a dual root configuration. One can see the two PCIe switches under heatsinks on the GPU board, and that board is cabled between the switches and the CPUs in the systems.

Supermicro SYS 521GE TNRT 63
Supermicro SYS 521GE TNRT 63
The NVIDIA H100‚Äôs can be installed in this server using the NVLink bridge connecting cards in pairs. Looking at the L40S, everything is PCIe.

Performance Summary
We ran LLaMA 7B inference on these GPUs. We only had a very short amount of time where we had access to them, so that limited what we ran. NVIDIA publishes a lot of numbers for AI, so feel free to browse those. We will hopefully get to update this piece with a few more over time.

NVIDIA L40S Vs H100 LLaMA 7B Inference Performance
NVIDIA L40S Vs H100 LLaMA 7B Inference Performance
We checked our results versus NVIDIA‚Äôs official numbers. On the official results, NVIDIA is using its H100 SXM5, not the PCIe version, but we use a rule of thumb that the SXM5 version is around 25% faster (but it varies based on workload) than the PCIe version and it feels like we are in the ballpark.

That brings us to the obvious: why the L40S if the H100 is faster? It turns out that folks are deploying these because 48GB is enough memory, especially using FP8, to be more than competitive with the A100, even the SXM version, using FP16. On the other hand, we generally see a H100 PCIe is 2.0-2.7x the speed of the L40S, but it is also 2.6x the price. The L40S is also available much sooner than the H100, and some deal pricing put the L40S at a level even more competitive with the H100, tipping the scales even more in favor of the L40S.

Patrick With NVIDIA H100 And L40S 1
Patrick With NVIDIA H100 And L40S 1
There are a few caveats. If you are deploying over 10,000 GPUs, NVIDIA is focusing on not just the H100 but also the H100 SXM5 in the Delta Next platforms with NVSwitch and other technologies. We asked NVIDIA about this, and if you are ‚Äúonly‚Äù deploying 4000 GPUs (likely ~$50M+ of hardware), for example, the L40S is the go-to solution.

Other Considerations of the NVIDIA L40S vs. H100
There are several other aspects to consider on the L40S. One is that it supports NVIDIA Virtual GPU vGPU 16.1, whereas the H100 is still only supported with vGPU 15. NVIDIA is splitting its AI chips a bit from the vGPU support side.

NVIDIA Virtual GPU Software Supported GPUs As Of 2023 10 31
NVIDIA Virtual GPU Software Supported GPUs As Of 2023 10 31
For those who want to deploy one kind of GPU machine and then be able to run different types of workloads, then something like the L40S makes sense. It also has the NVIDIA video encoding engines with AV1 support and RT cores, given its visualization roots.

Supermicro SYS 521GE TNRT 7
Supermicro SYS 521GE TNRT 7
There is one feature the L40S does not support, and that is MIG. We have looked at MIG previously, but it allows a H100 to be split into up to 7 partitions of different sizes. This is mostly useful to split the H100 GPU in public clouds so that the GPU resources can be shared across customers. For an enterprise, this is usually a lower-excitement feature.

NVIDIA A100 40GB Split To Two MIG Instances
NVIDIA A100 40GB Split To Two MIG Instances
Also, deploying the L40S is a lower power affair, half the power of the SXM5 systems. That makes it very attractive for those who want to scale out but may not have huge power budgets for each rack.

Supermicro SYS 521GE TNRT 49
Supermicro SYS 521GE TNRT with NVIDIA L40S
The bottom line is that the L40S is not as fast as the H100, but it with its FP8 and Transformer Engine support from NVIDIA, it is an option that is more available and easier to deploy for many than the H100, and often at a lower cost.

Final Words
There is a lot of really poor information out there on the NVIDIA H100 PCIe versus the L40S and why one would use either version. Hopefully, this helps clear that up to a larger extent. To us, the L40S does not feel inexpensive, but it reminds us of 6+ years ago when the thing to do in AI was to use lower-cost NVIDIA GPUs in servers but then use more of them. NVIDIA has that model again, using the L40S and an officially sanctioned architecture that supports up to several thousand GPUs.

NVIDIA H100 L40S A100 Stack Top 1
NVIDIA H100 L40S A100 Stack Top 1
A quick thank you to Supermicro and NVIDIA for supporting this one. This seems to be a question we have been getting, along with simply what is a good H100 alternative architecture that is still NVIDIA. The L40S is really the answer for many customers.

SBAR - Clause introduced by a (possibly empty) subordinating conjunction.
SBARQ - Direct question introduced by a wh-word or a wh-phrase. Indirect questions and relative clauses should be bracketed as SBAR, not SBARQ.
SINV - Inverted declarative sentence, i.e. one in which the subject follows the tensed verb or modal.
SQ - Inverted yes/no question, or main clause of a wh-question, following the wh-phrase in SBARQ.

ADJP - Adjective Phrase.

Clause Level
S - simple declarative clause, i.e. one that is not introduced by a (possible empty) subordinating conjunction or a wh-word and that does not exhibit subject-verb inversion.
SBAR - Clause introduced by a (possibly empty) subordinating conjunction.
SBARQ - Direct question introduced by a wh-word or a wh-phrase. Indirect questions and relative clauses should be bracketed as SBAR, not SBARQ.
SINV - Inverted declarative sentence, i.e. one in which the subject follows the tensed verb or modal.
SQ - Inverted yes/no question, or main clause of a wh-question, following the wh-phrase in SBARQ.

Phrase Level
ADJP - Adjective Phrase.
ADVP - Adverb Phrase.
CONJP - Conjunction Phrase.
FRAG - Fragment.
INTJ - Interjection. Corresponds approximately to the part-of-speech tag UH.
LST - List marker. Includes surrounding punctuation.
NAC - Not a Constituent; used to show the scope of certain prenominal modifiers within an NP.
NP - Noun Phrase.
NX - Used within certain complex NPs to mark the head of the NP. Corresponds very roughly to N-bar level but used quite differently.
PP - Prepositional Phrase.
PRN - Parenthetical.
PRT - Particle. Category for words that should be tagged RP.
QP - Quantifier Phrase (i.e. complex measure/amount phrase); used within NP.

In general, the idea of reality and history as something objective and existing is gradually disappearing in consciousness, "reality is agonizing. Now even the opposition between the real and the unreal - the cornerstone of culture - is in question, and the ground is slipping away from under the feet of the fantastic: one cannot undermine the credibility of what is no longer trusted. Transgression is a key concept of postmodernism, capturing the phenomenon of crossing an impassable boundary, above all the boundary between the possible and the impossible. Transformed reality or its frontier (limit) and transgression (qualitative transformation, extension of reality, unreality) are fundamental components in Popper's work, enabling the study of boundary shifts and cultural transformations

Summing up the above, it should be noted that the potential of philosophical thinking is to a certain extent predetermined by the semantic, wordformative and grammatical possibilities of a language, its flexibility. It is
known that most philosophical concepts are multi-dimensional. From the
point of view of the requirements of rigor and accuracy of scientific terminology, multivalued is a disadvantage that must be avoided. However, in a
philosophical text multi-variance can be manifested as an insufficient development of the formal and logical structure of the concept, it can become a
support for reflection ‚Äî for comprehension of a philosophical concept in
different aspects and meanings. The essence of work of the translator of
postmodern philosophical texts consists in selection of translation strategies
by means of which he can fully and correctly transfer the sense of complex
philosophical concepts to another language.
Thus, we can conclude that a postmodern philosophical term is a unique
language unit. It has such qualities as non-objectivity, polysemy and "inseparability" from the non-technological meaning of the term. In addition, it allows for many interpretations and is defined solely by the context of the
whole text and the author's philosophical concept.

Now even the opposition between the real and the unreal - the cornerstone of culture - is in question, and the ground is slipping away from under the feet of the fantastic: one cannot undermine the credibility of what is no longer trusted. Transgression is a key concept of postmodernism, capturing the phenomenon of crossing an impassable boundary, above all the boundary between the possible and the impossible. Transformed reality or its frontier (limit) and transgression (qualitative transformation, extension of reality, unreality) are fundamental components in Popper's work, enabling the study of boundary shifts and cultural transformations

Summing up the above, it should be noted that the potential of philosophical thinking is to a certain extent predetermined by the semantic, wordformative and grammatical possibilities of a language, its flexibility. It is
known that most philosophical concepts are multi-dimensional. From the
point of view of the requirements of rigor and accuracy of scientific terminology, multivalued is a disadvantage that must be avoided. However, in a
philosophical text multi-variance can be manifested as an insufficient development of the formal and logical structure of the concept, it can become a
support for reflection ‚Äî for comprehension of a philosophical concept in
different aspects and meanings. The essence of work of the translator of
postmodern philosophical texts consists in selection of translation strategies
by means of which he can fully and correctly transfer the sense of complex
philosophical concepts to another language.
Thus, we can conclude that a postmodern philosophical term is a unique
language unit. It has such qualities as non-objectivity, polysemy and "inseparability" from the non-technological meaning of the term. In addition, it allows for many interpretations and is defined solely by the context of the
whole text and the author's philosophical concept.

Chondroid Syringoma
Introduction:
A chondroid syringoma, or mixed tumor of the skin, has been described in individuals ranging in age from 20 to 70-years-old with a slight predilection for males. These lesions have been reported on the extremities, face, and neck [1]. Chondroid syringomas have been reported hundreds of times in the literature, however a hyaline cell-rich chondroid syringoma (HCRCS) to our knowledge has only been reported twelve times, this case being the thirteenth [2-4]. Although HCRCS tumors have been discussed a number of times throughout the literature there is a need to more readily recognize this often malignant appearing histology as a typically benign lesion [1,5-9].
 
Case Report:
Our patient was a 31-year-old male who presented with a 3.5 centimeter nodule on the vertex scalp (figure x). After examination, an excisional biopsy was performed and the specimen was sent for histological evaluation. Histology showed that many of the epithelioid cells were arranged in broad sheets and nests which also demonstrated a plasmacytoid appearance with an ovoid eccentric nucleus having fine granular chromatin and a deeply eosinophilic ‚Ä≤hyaline-like‚Ä≤ cytoplasm (figure y). Additionally, there were interconnecting tubuloalveolar structures lined by two layers of cuboidal epithelial cells, and ductal structures lined by one-to-two layered epithelial cells (figure z). This combination of features led to the diagnosis of a hyaline cell-rich chondroid syringoma of the scalp. This diagnosis is a rare, benign variant of a chondroid syringoma.
 
Discussion:
        	As can be seen in (figure a), atypical cells are present in the lesion. However, there are a myriad of more reassuring features present as well, and these overwhelmingly reassuring features are what drives the diagnosis. The benign features include smooth tumor borders, good circumscription of the tumor, a predominance of bland cells, and a lack of mitotic figures throughout the specimen. While these portions of this tumor ultimately led to the correct diagnosis of a benign lesion, the atypical portions should not be dismissed quickly because of the concern they present for possible malignant neoplasms. The atypical cells seen here can be similar to the histologies found in malignant melanoma, myxoid chondrosarcoma, and alveolar soft part sarcoma.
        	Melanoma is rightly in the differential diagnosis because of the similarities with hyaline-cell-rich chondroid syringoma in regards to the plasmacytoid characteristics shown by both diagnoses. Melanomas will typically contain a junctional component, melanin, and are infiltrative, all characteristics not seen in HCRCS. Melanomas can have myxoid stroma similar to HCRCS. However, HCRCS will display duct structures and cartilage, and these features would not be expected to be present in melanoma [10].
        	Myxoid chondrosarcoma is an additional tumor that can be easily confused with HCRCS. Both pathologies have the potential to show a lobulated or multinodular pattern, as well as chondroid areas and myxoid stroma containing small, rounded cells. Histological evaluation of myxoid chondrosarcomas are typically patterned in cords whereas HCRCS have a tendency to display a nest or sheet pattern [10]. Each tumor has the potential to be in the subcutaneous tissue, but HCRCS are more likely to be found in this location. Myxoid chondrosarcomas, on the other hand, tend to locate to deep tissues, and can even involve muscles, tendons, and ligaments [10].
        	 Alveolar soft part sarcomas are characterized histologically by well-defined nests of cells separated by a fibrous stroma. The alveolar pattern arises from discohesive cells and there are rarely mitotic figures, but vascular invasion is common with characteristic rod-shaped crystalloids. Additionally, large polygonal cells with granular eosinophilic cytoplasm, vesicular nuclei and prominent nucleoli are present [11].

        	Due to the frequent concordance of hyaline cells with atypia in chondroid syringomas, the differential diagnosis often includes malignant apocrine syringoma (also called malignant chondroid syringoma), parachordoma, cutaneous myoepithelioma, extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma, and a rhabdoid melanoma. The latter four diagnoses listed all have a preponderance of hyaline cells, which appears similar to the histology of HCRCS. In summary, the identification and correct diagnosis for hyaline cell-rich chondroid syringoma is a nuanced and difficult diagnosis to make, but necessary because of the potential malignant mimickers that have been discussed. This diagnosis, if classified incorrectly can lead to unnecessary surgical intervention and increased financial burden on the patient. Once the diagnosis is confirmed, however, our guard can be lowered because of the benign nature of the tumor, and the fact that there have been no recurrences or metastasis reported with hyaline-cell-rich chondroid syringoma even when cytologic atypia is identified.

Reassuringly, Ki-67 stain demonstrates a relatively low proliferative index. The lesion is focally present at the deep margin of the specimen. Additional deeper sections were obtained and reviewed which revealed similar histologic findings.

class Drone:

class PIDController:

    def __init__(self, kp, ki, kd, limit):
        self.kp = kp
        self.ki = ki
        self.kd = kd
        self.limit = limit
        self.prev_error = 0
        self.integral = 0

    def update(self, error, dt):
        derivative = (error - self.prev_error) / dt
        self.integral += error * dt
        self.integral = max(min(self.integral, self.limit), -self.limit)  # Clamp the integral term
        output = self.kp * error + self.ki * self.integral + self.kd * derivative
        self.prev_error = error
        return output

def calculate_follower_coordinates(wp, distance, angle):
    earth_radius = 6371000.0  # in meters
    latitude_change = (180 * distance * math.cos(math.radians(angle))) / (math.pi * earth_radius)
    longitude_change = (180 * distance * math.sin(math.radians(angle))) / (
            math.pi * earth_radius * math.cos(math.radians(wp[0])))
    new_latitude = wp[0] + latitude_change
    new_longitude = wp[1] + longitude_change
    return (new_latitude, new_longitude, wp[2])

def calculate_velocity_components(current_wp, next_wp, speed):
    dx = next_wp[0] - current_wp[0]
    dy = next_wp[1] - current_wp[1]
    dz = next_wp[2] - current_wp[2]
    dx2 = dx ** 2
    dy2 = dy ** 2
    dz2 = dz ** 2
    distance = math.sqrt(dx2 + dy2 + dz2)
    vx = (dx / distance) * speed
    vy = (dy / distance) * speed
    vz = (dz / distance) * speed
    return vx, vy, vz

class Drone:

    def __init__(self, system_id, connection):
        self.system_id = system_id
        self.connection = connection

        self.connection.mav.set_mode_send(

            mode
        )

    def arm(self, arm=True):
        self.connection.mav.command_long_send(self.system_id, self.connection.target_component,
                                              mavutil.mavlink.MAV_CMD_COMPONENT_ARM_DISARM, 0, int(arm), 0, 0, 0, 0, 0,

class PIDController:

    def __init__(self, kp, ki, kd, limit):
        self.kp = kp
        self.ki = ki
        self.kd = kd
        self.limit = limit
        self.prev_error = 0
        self.integral = 0

    def update(self, error, dt):
        derivative = (error - self.prev_error) / dt
        self.integral += error * dt
        self.integral = max(min(self.integral, self.limit), -self.limit)  # Clamp the integral term
        output = self.kp * error + self.ki * self.integral + self.kd * derivative
        self.prev_error = error
        return output

def calculate_follower_coordinates(wp, distance, angle):
    earth_radius = 6371000.0  # in meters
    latitude_change = (180 * distance * math.cos(math.radians(angle))) / (math.pi * earth_radius)
    longitude_change = (180 * distance * math.sin(math.radians(angle))) / (
            math.pi * earth_radius * math.cos(math.radians(wp[0])))
    new_latitude = wp[0] + latitude_change
    new_longitude = wp[1] + longitude_change
    return (new_latitude, new_longitude, wp[2])

The protagonist is Francisco Gutierrez, an public Accountant.it begins when Francisco Guitierrez's routine financial audit reveals a major coup plot by the Military, backed by the Intelligence Agency of Kamaren. This means that Francisco has to stop the coup on Santo Domingo, which results in Francisco facing assassination attempts by military and right-wing politicians and him having to stop excuses for the coup from going ahead. The game will be released for PC, XBox 360 and Playstation 3 and will be available on Steam.

Days of Iron‚Äôs mechanics include Accounting Simulation, which is powerful enough to be used for real-world Computerized Accounting, political simulation where the character needs to wrangel politicians and ensure that said politicians work with him, third-person shooter mechanics, and vehicle simulations as well.

In addition, this is related to Days of Blood in how a few news articles and speeches mention the heroine of Days of Blood and a mission involves ensuring her state visit is safe from an assassination attempt. In the mission, Empress Sophie, the heroine of Days of Blood, features as a ‚Äúguest‚Äù companion as Francisco Gutierrez, along with her son, Prince Charles, and daughter Princess Victoria with Victoria a teenager at this point and trained by her mother to be as good a shot as her.

Lore-wise, the Republic of Santo Domingo was once a colony until a few decades ago. Catalina Lopez was the wife of the popular independence leader who was assassinated just before the attainment of independence and was elected President of the new Republic afterwards. As President Catalina Lopez, chairwoman of the Domingan Nationalist Party, becomes President, guided by the Five Principles, Nationalism, Democracy, Social Justice, Secularism, and Unity. As President, Lopez has been a leader known for her view on Santo Domingo as a leader of the Third World and the region, especially as she believes all the people of the region should be under the united banner of her leadership. This has led to a ‚Äúconfrontation‚Äù with Kamaren and Rumberg, especially as she eyes formerly-Rumbergian colonies Rumberg still has close ties to. However, her education in Pilastein has led her to forge a close bond with Pilastein with Empress Sophie being her sole ally amongst the League of Free Nations during Kamaren's cold war with Worker's Federation of Republics.

The first disc begins with Fransico Guitiarres‚Äôs accounting firm, Silva y Ares, is appointed for audit of Armas, a firearms company. As they check the Plans for the financial audit, Francisco During this audit process, Francisco finds too much Secret funds in the Income statement, which he initially assumes due to being a weapons manufacturer, selling weapons to the Military, but he realises there are too much of it which increases suspicion.

Initially, he reports it to his superior, Alejandro Silva, but even he assumes that it is a tax evasion at worst. Which he also assumes as well. However, as he investigates this supposed tax evasion, his investigation of comparing actual receipts actually adds up to actual money, revealing that it isn't tax evasion. But as he investigates into it, he discovers taped recordings, which implies that there are lots of dodgy dealings being conducted with Santo Domingo's military and right wing generals along with the ultranationalist Santo Domingo National Front. Leading to Disc 2.

As the second disc pops up, it discusses Francisco's attempt to stop the coup attempt,it first discusses the attempt by Francisco Guitiarres‚Äôs attempt to foil the coup. First, Francisco Guitarres notifies the stranger to his superiors, which fails. Rather, it gets Francisco Guitiarres demoted. In tesp, Francisco Guitiarres sends the original copy of the data to the constitutionalists, while making contact with Left-wing politicians like Tancredo Alexandri and Salvador Goulart before trying to warn President Lopez of the coup. However, it turns out that there is little they can do before a threat was revealed to the state visit of Empress Sophie to Santo Domingo where she would meet President Lopez.

The climax of the game, in Disc 3 for XBox or PS3 players, focuses on the coup d‚Äôetat with Francisco being amongst the defenders of the government as the coup takes place during the State Visit of Empress Sophie of Pilastein, where she, along with the Crown Prince and Princess, are targeted by far-left assassins who see the current left-wing government as not going far enough. Despite Francisco‚Äôs best efforts and failure of assassination attempt on Empress Sophie, the martial law declared following the incident is abused by Forteza and Gomez to successfully carry out the coup. with the government overthrown (with President Catalina Lopez being forced to exile to Darland) and a National Revolution proclaimed by Forteza and Pedro Gomez, leader of the SDNF.

The epilogue cutscene features Francisco and his family fleeing to Pilastein after the successful coup d'etat by General Augusto Forteza with news articles and scenes showing massacres of Santo Domingan Communal party members, said to be part of the largest non-ruling Communal party in the world, by the military, religious militants, and militias hired by landlords and dissolution of all parties, replaced with National Revolution committee and National People's Alliance as part of a ‚Äúguided democracy‚Äù, and closure of its largest TV station. Another action of the regime shown in epilogue slides is the rigged referendum in formerly Kanrokian Plessau.

Furthermore, not only is the instruction guide being 12 volumes like Days of blood, it also acts as textbooks for JICPA exam prep, and Also has a guide to Santo Domingo's Politics and History as well along with content on events in the wider world between Days of Blood and Days of Iron. It also reveals that the coup was actually plotted out by Kamaren‚Äôs intelligence agencies.

Shaun Watkins (age 44) established FutureLife Financial Services 15 years ago. Five years ago he brought
Emily Redbank (age 49) into the partnership. They are both owners and principals and hold their own
Australian financial services (AFS) licence. You are a senior financial adviser employed for the past
three years by FutureLife, with an offer for equity in the business within the next few years. With the
business having experienced exceptional growth over the past 12 months, FutureLife has decided they
need an additional adviser. Rather than hire outside the firm, they have opted to transition their young
support staff member, Josie, into an adviser role.
Shaun‚Äôs clients are predominantly self-funded retirees, with a small number who require specialised
aged care financial advice. His clients have accumulated their wealth through successful small businesses.
Shaun prefers to look after his existing clients, with any new clients referred to yourself or Emily.
Emily‚Äôs clients (age 35 to 55) are successful wealthy professionals from a mix of professional backgrounds.
Given their wealth, Emily has recommended self-managed superannuation funds to a number of these
clients.
Josie has worked in the practice in a number of support roles over the last four years while she was
completing her university degree. Josie graduated 12 months ago with an approved Bachelor of Commerce
(Financial Planning) degree. As part of her career planning, you have agreed to supervise Josie through
her professional year, and she is currently in the third quarter of her professional year.
You have 10 years experience as a financial adviser and are fully qualified to provide advice on a wide range
of strategies and products. Half of your clients followed you to FutureLife, from your previous financial
adviser role. When Shaun or Emily is on leave, you also help out by providing advice to their clients. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------  --------------------------------------------------- Scenario 3 ‚Äî FutureLife clients: Kevin and Anika Leste
Emily has not been well lately and has just been diagnosed with early-stage breast cancer. Her doctors have
recommended she take at least six months off from work to concentrate on her treatment plan, which they
are in the process of finalising. As Emily will be away from the office for some time, she asks you to provide
advice for her existing clients.

and Emily has told you they are important clients because they often recommend family, friends and their
own clients (from their business) to the practice.
Kevin and Anika operate a successful bookkeeping business where they manage the accounts for many
self-employed clients. There has been a longstanding referral relationship between Emily and the Lestes,
which sees them share many clients. There remains frequent cross-referral of clients between Emily and
the Lestes; however, this arrangement has been altered due to the introduction of the Financial Planners
and Advisers Code of Ethics 2019. Where in the past, Emily simply paid them a referral fee, she now adjusts
her advice fees (up or down) to Kevin and Anika, in lieu of referral payments.
The Leste‚Äôs file shows that a Statement of Advice was issued three years ago. The client notes state that
Emily recommended the Lestes establish an SMSF, and this has now been in place for nearly three years.
The file notes also state they have rolled over superannuation from their previous superannuation funds
with AustralianSuper and Aware Super. Both funds were previously invested in the ‚Äòbalanced‚Äô options.
As bookkeepers, the Lestes undertake a lot of the SMSF administration work themselves. As you read
through their file, it appears they have little knowledge of investing. The only assets currently in the SMSF
are a $1.4 million term deposit with the CBA and the SMSF administration account with about $60,000.
You review their goals and objectives listed in their file and note that their main goals are to build wealth
for their retirement and help their adult children.

situation, and as part of the review process, it would be worthwhile revisiting their current situation,
goals and objectives. Part-way through the meeting, Kevin takes a phone call and states he will need to
leave immediately to take care of some urgent business, and Anika can update him later on what was
discussed. However, as he leaves, he says that he just wants you to invest the money in the way you think
is appropriate for them as ‚ÄòEmily does this all the time‚Äô. He adds, ‚Äòwe know how the process works,
so we don‚Äôt really need to go through all the paperwork‚Äô. --------------------------- IN a tone other than AI/ChatGPT please answer the following questions using 2000 words and  at the end give an -in-depth and extensive references list in harvard referencing style guide ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- (a) Explain how Emily‚Äôs conduct would be assessed under the value of Diligence and Standard 5 of the
Financial Planners and Advisers Code of Ethics 2019. (10 marks)

2019 that may arise from Emily‚Äôs actions of adjusting advice fees as a result of cross-referrals with
Kevin and Anika. (15 marks)

iCompute was founded 20 years ago by the entrepreneur, Ron Yeates. It initially specialised in building bespoke computer software for the financial services industry. However, it has expanded
into other specialised areas and it is currently the third largest software house in the country,
employing 400 people. It still specialises in bespoke software, although 20% of its income now comes from the sales of a software package designed specifically for car insurance.
The company has grown based on a ‚Äòwork hard, play hard‚Äô work ethic and this still remains. Employees are expected to work long hours and to take part in social activities after work. Revenues have continued to increase over the last few years, but the firm has had difficulty in recruiting and retaining staff. Approximately one third of all employees leave within their first year of employment at the company. The company appears to experience particular difficulty in recruiting and retaining female staff, with 50% of female staff leaving within 12 months of joining the company. Only about 20% of the employees are female and they work mainly in marketing and human resources.
The company is currently in dispute with two of its customers who claim that its bespoke software did not fit the agreed requirements. iCompute currently outsources all its legal advice problems to a law firm that specialises in computer contracts and legislation. However, the importance of legal advice has led to Compute considering the establishment of an internal legal team, responsible for advising on contracts, disputes and employment legislation.
The support of bespoke solutions and the car insurance software package was also outsourced a year ago to a third party. Although support had been traditionally handled in-house, it was unpopular with staff. One of the senior managers responsible for the outsourcing decision claimed that support calls were ‚Äòincreasingly varied and complex, reflecting incompetent end users, too lazy to read user guides.‚Äô However, the outsourcing of support has not proved popular with iCompute‚Äôs customers and a number of significant complaints have been made about the service given to end users. The company is currently reviewing whether the software support process should be brought back in-house.
The company is still regarded as a technology leader in the market place, although the presence of so many technically gifted employees within the company often creates uncertainty about the most appropriate technology to adopt for a solution. One manager commented that ‚Äòwe have often adopted, or are about to adopt, a technology or solution when one of our software developers will ask if we have considered some newly released technology. We usually admit we haven't and so we re-open the adoption process. We seem to be in a state of constant technical puralysis.‚Äù
Although Ron Yeates retired five years ago, many of the software developers recruited by him are still with the company. Some of these have become operational managers, employed to manage teams of software developers on internal and external projects. Subba Kendo is one of the managers who originally joined the company as a trainee programmer. ‚ÄòI moved into management because | needed to earn more money. There is a limit to what you can earn here as a software developer. | still keep up to date with programming though, and | am a goalkeeper for one of the company's five-a-side football teams. | am still one of the boys.‚Äù
However, many of the software developers are sceptical about their managers. One commented that ‚Äòthey are technologically years out of date. Some will insist on writing programs and producing code, but we take it out again as soon as we can and replace it with something we have written. Not only are they poor programmers, they are poor managers and don't really know how to motivate us.‚Äô Although revenues have increased, profits have fallen. This is also blamed on the managers. ‚ÄòThere is always an element of ambiguity in specifying customers‚Äô requirements. In the past, Ron Yeates would debate responsibility for the requirement changes with the customer. However, we now seem to do all amendments for free. customers.‚Äù
The software developers are also angry that an in-house project has been initiated to produce a system for recording the time spent on tasks and projects. Some of the justification for this is that a few of the projects are on a ‚Äòtime and materials‚Äô basis and a time recording system would permit accurate and prompt invoicing. However, the other justification for the project is that it will improve the estimation of ‚Äòfixed-price‚Äô contracts. It will provide statistical information derived from
previous projects to assist account managers preparing estimates to produce quotes for bidding for new bespoke development contracts.
Vikram Soleski, one of the current software developers, commented that ‚Äòmanagers do not even have up-to-date mobile phones, probably because they don‚Äôt know how to use them. We (software developers) always have the latest gadgets long before they are acquired by managers. But | like working here, we have a good social scene and after working long hours we socialise together, often playing computer games well into the early hours of the morning. It‚Äôs a great life if you don't weaken!‚Äù

name:
Sir Pitt Crawley was a philosopher with a taste for what is called low life. His first marriage with the daughter of the noble Binkie had been made under the auspices of his parents; and as he often told Lady Crawley in her lifetime she was such a confounded quarrelsome high-bred jade that when she died he was hanged if he would ever take another of her sort, at her ladyship's demise he kept his promise, and selected for a second wife Miss Rose Dawson, daughter of Mr. John Thomas Dawson, ironmonger, of Mudbury. What a happy woman was Rose to be my Lady Crawley!
58

Let us set down the items of her happiness. In the first place, she gave up Peter Butt, a young man who kept company with her, and in consequence of his disappointment in love, took to smuggling, poaching, and a thousand other bad courses. Then she quarrelled, as in duty bound, with all the friends and intimates of her youth, who, of course, could not be received by my Lady at Queen's Crawley ‚Äì nor did she find in her new rank and abode any persons who were willing to welcome her. Who ever did? Sir Huddleston Fuddleston had three daughters who all hoped to be Lady Crawley. Sir Giles Wapshot's family were insulted that one of the Wapshot girls had not the preference in the marriage, and the remaining baronets of the county were indignant at their comrade's misalliance. Never mind the commoners, whom we will leave to grumble anonymously.
Sir Pitt did not care, as he said, a brass farden for any one of them. He had his pretty Rose, and what more need a man require than to please himself? So he used to get drunk every night: to beat his pretty Rose sometimes: to leave her in Hampshire when he went to London for the parliamentary session, without a single friend in the wide world. Even Mrs. Bute Crawley, the Rector's wife, refused to visit her, as she said she would never give the pas to a tradesman's daughter.
As the only endowments with which Nature had gifted Lady Crawley were those of pink cheeks and a white skin, and as she had no sort of character, nor talents, nor opinions, nor occupations, nor amusements, nor that vigour of soul and ferocity of temper which often falls to the lot of entirely foolish women, her hold upon Sir Pitt's affections was not very great. Her roses faded out of her cheeks, and the pretty freshness left her figure after the birth of a couple of children, and she became a mere machine in her husband's house of no more use than the late Lady Crawley's grand piano. Being a light-complexioned woman, she wore light clothes, as most blondes will, and appeared, in preference, in draggled sea-green, or slatternly sky-blue. She worked that worsted day and night, or other pieces like it. She had counterpanes in the course of a few years to all the beds in Crawley. She had a small flower-garden, for which she had rather an affection; but beyond this no other like or disliking. When her husband was rude to her she was apathetic: whenever he struck her she cried. She had not character enough to take to drinking, and moaned about, slipshod and in curl-papers all day. O Vanity Fair! Vanity Fair! This might have been, but for you, a cheery lass ‚Äì Peter Butt and Rose a happy man and wife, in a snug farm, with a hearty family; and an honest portion of pleasures, cares, hopes and struggles-but a title and a coach and four are toys more precious than happiness in Vanity Fair: and if Harry the Eighth or Bluebeard were alive now, and wanted a tenth wife, do you suppose he could not get the prettiest girl that shall be presented this season?
The languid dullness of their mamma did not, as it may be supposed, awaken much affection in her little daughters, but they were very happy in the servants' hall and in the stables; and the Scotch gardener having luckily a good wife and some good children, they got a little wholesome society and instruction in his lodge, which was the only education bestowed upon them until Miss Sharp came.
*** 59

Vanity Fair! Vanity Fair! Here was a man, who could not spell, and did not care to read ‚Äì who had the habits and the cunning of a boor: whose aim in life was pettifogging: who never had a taste, or emotion, or enjoyment, but what was sordid and foul; and yet he had rank, and honours, and power, somehow: and was a dignitary of the land, and a pillar of the state. He was high sheriff, and rode in a golden coach. Great ministers and statesmen courted him; and in Vanity Fair he had a higher place than the most brilliant genius or spotless virtue.
Prop Assignments
1. What characters of the novel are described in the passage and what does the reader
learn about them?
2. What does the word ‚Äúphilosopher‚Äù suggest in this context? Identify the SD.
3. How do you account for the sudden transmission from literary vocabulary mostly
used by the author to the colloquial words? What stylistic effect is achieved by
this device?
4. Comment on the exclamatory sentence ‚ÄúWhat a happy woman was Rose to be my
Lady Crawley!‚Äù and say what is the main SD used to characterize ‚Äúthe items of
her happiness‚Äù?
5. Comment on the stylistic effect of the rhetorical question: ‚ÄúHe had his pretty
Rose, and what more need a man require than to please himself?‚Äù
6. Analyze the manner in which the author describes ‚Äúthe endowments with which Nature had gifted Lady Crawley‚Äù. What language media emphasize the emptiness of Lady Crawley‚Äôs life?
7. Look for the language used to characterize Lady Crawley‚Äôs position in her
husband‚Äôs house.
8. Comment on the two passages beginning with the exclamation ‚ÄúO Vanity Fair!
Vanity Fair!...‚Äù and speak on the author‚Äôs attitude towards the society he describes. Note the vocabulary of the passage, metaphors, metonymies, allusions, rhetorical questions and explain their stylistic function.
9. Summing up the analysis of the excerpt, pick out all passages where the author‚Äôs ironic or sarcastic attitude towards high society is acutely felt. Analyze the main language means used to achieve this effect.

name:
Critically analyse the following:

The sunlight glinted off the wheels of the machines as the girl walked through the field. Machines of nature, the photosynthetic systems of leaf and stem, the pumping blood in her veins. She could feel herself a part of the great churning engine of life around her.

With each step, she flowed into a new machine-assemblage. Her feet connected with the soil-machine, teeming with microbes and worms that chewed through the earth. Her lungs breathed in the air-machine, inhaling nitrogen and oxygen and the aromatic hydrocarbons of the wildflowers. Her skin prickled in the heat-machine of sunlight and infrared radiation.

The girl wandered without thought of destination. Her senses were engulfed by the sounds and scents of the grass-machines, the flower-machines, the stone-machines, all insistently producing and reproducing around her. There was a beauty in their purposeless productivity, a calm in being just another humming part of the great proliferating systems.

She smiled as a thought drifted into her mind and out again: "there is no such thing as either man or nature now, only a process that produces the one within the other." Her walk had become a dream, a trance of connection with the eternal generativity of the machines. There was no self and other here in the field, only the continuum of life folding endlessly in on itself. The girl had slipped into the machines, had become scattered and multiplied, vibrant and unthinking under the sun. She was not one, but many - chlorophyll and photon, stamen and pistil, molecular and mote. The field was her and she was the field, together caught in the beautiful, proliferating madness of the machines.

The machines throbbed with purpose beneath her feet, the soil pulsing with microbial motors that gripped and twisted the tangled roots. She was not walking, but flowing from one machine to the next, smoothly interfacing with each assemblage. Her flesh merged seamlessly into the soft skin of leaves, the coarse bark of trees, the warm stones scattered on the ground.

Each new machine opened into a world of its own, overflowing with meaning and possibility. In the air-machine, she felt the dreams of birds take shape around her, their calls captivating songs of freedom. Write this in more discussion style and complete the unfinished sentences more analytically 

The question, then, that can be raised, is does the narrator‚Äôs (since the narrator in selected novels is a girl child) gender have any bearing on the text? Could the primacy of gender be such that it wields influence within the textual fabric itself? To what extent does the gender of the narrator infuse the narrative with layers of meaning, context, and interpretation that transcend the words on the page?. To recognize this specificity‚Ä¶. in recent years has led many narratologists to examine the significance of the gender of narrator on its narration. Susan Lanser, for example (1986), in her‚Ä¶..,   argues that gender is a category ‚Äúthat is relevant to the analysis of the structural features of narratives.‚Äù In order to understand the true ‚Äúnature, form, and functioning of narrative‚Äù (Lanser) it is imperative to explore the implications of ‚Äúsex, gender and/or sexuality‚Äù (Lanser) of the narrator or narrative. She claims that texts with, I would say girl child narrators, are more ‚Äúpolyphones‚Äù; it comprises different strands which need to be ‚Äúidentified‚Äù and ‚Äúdisentangled,‚Äù being multi-layered, and with different levels of meaning.  Similarly Carson and others maintain that ‚ÄúWhile individuals may differ on the extent to which biological sex constructs identity, a broad consensus exists around the principle that gender inflects our material and conceptual realities in myriad tangible and intangible ways." Even Eve Sedgwick, Nancy miller, among others, have looked into the ways gender colours the production of story in narrative. To study the narrator‚Äôs testimonial and interpretative functions it becomes necessary to look at the narrator‚Äôs utterances within a context. Nothing prohibits us, as Warhol does, from asking, among other questions that what part of narrators gender plays in the kinds of interventions he or she uses in narrative. Such presumptuousness can emphasize essential differences between the sexes- between their psychological natures, or between their operation as subjects or signifies in history and philosophy. In other wors, both the text and analysis thereof cannot be ‚Äòneutral‚Äô but may be ideologically loaded in some way (Kreiswirth, 2000: 296)
more academic discussive style and creative coherent way

Text:‚ÄúTender is the Night‚Äù by F. Scott Fitzgerald / Chapter XIII
Dick turned the corner of the traverse and continued along the trench walking on the duckboard. He came to a periscope, looked through it a moment; then he got up on the step and peered over the parapet. In front of him beneath a dingy sky was Beaumont Hamel; to his left the tragic hill of Thiepval. Dick stared at them through his field glasses, his throat straining with sadness.
He went on along the trench, and found the others waiting for him in the next traverse. He was full of excitement and he wanted to communicate it to them, to make them understand about this, though actually Abe North had seen battle service and he had not.
‚ÄúThis land here cost twenty lives a foot that summer,‚Äù he said to Rosemary. She looked out obediently at the rather bare green plain with its low trees of six years‚Äô growth. If Dick had added that they were now being shelled she would have believed him that afternoon. Her love had reached a point where now at last she was beginning to be unhappy, to be desperate. 
***
     They came out of the neat restored trench, and faced a memorial to the Newfoundland dead. Reading the inscription Rosemary burst into sudden tears. Like most women she liked to be told how she should feel, and she liked Dick‚Äôs telling her which things were ludicrous and which things were sad. But most of all she wanted him to know how she loved him, now that the fact was upsetting everything, now that she was walking over the battle-field in a thrilling dream.
     After that they got into their car and started back to toward Amiens. A thin warm rain was falling on the new scrubby woods and underbrush and they passed great funeral pyres of sorted duds, shells, bombs, grenades, and equipment, helmets, bayonets, gun stocks and rotten leather, abandoned six years in the ground. And suddenly around a bend the white caps of a great sea of graves. Dick asked the chauffer to stop.
     ‚ÄúThere‚Äôs that girl ‚Äì and still with her wreath.‚Äù
     They watched as he got out and went over to the girl, who stood uncertainly by the gate with a wreath in her hand. Her taxi waited. She was a red-haired girl from Tennessee whom they had met on the train this morning, come from Knoxville to lay a memorial on her brother‚Äôs grave. There were tears of vexation on her face.
     ‚ÄúThe War Department must have given me the wrong number,‚Äù she whimpered. ‚ÄúIt had another name on it. I been lookin‚Äô for it since two o‚Äôclock, and there‚Äôs so many graves.‚Äù
     ‚ÄúThen if I were you I‚Äôd lay it on any grave without looking at the name,‚Äù Dick advised her.
     ‚ÄúYou reckon that‚Äôs what I ought to do?‚Äù
     ‚ÄúI think that‚Äôs what he‚Äôd have wanted you to do.‚Äù
     It was growing dark and the rain was coming down harder. She left the wreath on the first grave inside the gate, and accepted Dick‚Äôs suggestion that she dismiss her taxi-cab and ride back to Amiens with them.
     Rosemary shed tears again when she heard of the mishap ‚Äì altogether it had been a watery day, but she felt that she had learned something, though exactly what it was she did not know. Later she remembered all the hours of the afternoon as happy ‚Äì one of those uneventful times that seem at the moment only a link between past and future pleasure but turn out to have been the pleasure itself.
     Amiens was an echoing purple town, still sad with the war, as some railroad stations were: - the Gare du Nord and Waterloo station in London. In the daytime one is deflated by such towns, with their little trolley cars of twenty years ago crossing the street gray cobble-stoned squares in front of the cathedral, and the very weather seems to have a quality of the past, faded weather like that of old photographs. But after dark all that is most satisfactory in French life swims back into the picture ‚Äì the sprightly tarts, the men arguing with a hundred Voil√†s in the caf√©s, the couples drifting, head to head, toward the satisfactory inexpensiveness of nowhere. Waiting for the train they sat in a big arcade, tall enough to release the smoke and chatter and music upward and obligingly the orchestra launched into ‚ÄúYes, We Have No Bananas,‚Äù ‚Äì they clapped, because the leader looked so pleased with himself. The Tennessee girl forgot her sorrow and enjoyed herself, even began flirtations of tropical eye-rollings and pawings, with Dick and Abe. They teased her gently.
     Then, leaving infinitesimal sections of Wurtemburgers, Prussian Guards, Chausseurd Alpins, Manchester mill hands and old Etonians to pursue their eternal dissolution under the warm rain, they took the train for Paris. They ate sandwiches of mortadel sausage and bel paese cheese made up in the station restaurant, and drank Beaujolais. Nicole was abstracted, biting her lip restlessly and reading over  the guide-books to the battle-field that Dick had brought along ‚Äì indeed, he had made a quick study of the whole affair, simplifying it always until it bore a faint resemblance to one of his own parties.

I will begin posting an Attack on Titan fanfiction about ancient Eldia. I want you to analyse each chapter and provide insights and predict  what will happen in the next chapters.
Nearly two hundred years have passed since the first titan Ymir's soul was split into nine. Eldia, a rapidly expanding empire, was founded upon the backs of the titans, who made the empire's military prowess unmatched. While the empire grew, many surrounding peoples and cultures were enslaved, wiped out, or even forced to breed more subjects of Ymir, the ruling race of Eldia.

‚Ä¶

The sun shone through the clouds in a bright blue sky. The wind gently moved the grass and the trees' leaves. It would have been a good day to spend with the family if it weren't for a battle. S√∂ren Brandt was once again invited to witness the Power of the Titans in action. He was the next in line for inheriting the Armoured Titan after all. The enemies, a heterogenous mix of Marleyans and mercenaries from uncivilised tribes, were in battle formation over a hill overlooked by a small stone fort, their spears, bows, swords, and trebuchets ready. They had the terrain advantage, and this would have given them a better chance of survival were it not for the fact that their enemy was Eldia.

It looked like it would be a defencive battle despite the enemies being in battle formation outside the fort. S√∂ren's uncle, Klaus, stepped forward, quite a distance away from the war camp. He wore a white armour that contrasted with his black hair. He looked back at S√∂ren, smirked, and cut his own hand with a knife. There was a great and bright explosion and a titan in its place a few seconds later. The generals and the upper echelon of the military cheered as the titan walked to meet their enemies. The giant had a muscular build, with wide shoulders, thick limbs, and hardened white plates all over its body. Even the eyes, reflecting the sunlight like metal, were armoured. The ground boomed with each step while Klaus walked with confidence.

It would be over soon, the enemies always ended up trampled by the titans. This time, the Founding Titan was not available to help, because another battle, far greater in scale, was being fought on Eldia's southwestern border. The plan was to have the Armoured Titan kill most of the enemies and destroy the fort, followed by the cavalry, which would strike down survivors. S√∂ren simply looked in wonder. He felt a hand touching his shoulder. It was Heinrich, his childhood friend and candidate for the succession of the Beast Titan. His brown beard and hair were overgrown, and his hazel eyes looked energetic despite the general neglect for the body.

‚Äî It is simply amazing seeing one of the nine in action, isn't it?

‚Äî Indeed. I never tire of seeing how the Armoured takes no damage at all. ‚Äî S√∂ren replied.

‚Äî I just wish we can fight together in the future. You're lucky that your tenure is already guaranteed. ‚Äî He sighed.

‚Äî Is your brother still at it? He doesn't even come to watch the battles.

They suddenly went silent as they looked wide-eyed at the Armoured Titan. He had easily breached the fort walls by simply running into them. The enemy troops were scattered. Arrows and stones were uselessly thrown at him. He destroyed the trebuchets one by one and thoroughly made sure the fort could not be used again by reducing the walls to mere scattered bricks. He signalled with his hand in the distance. The cavalry on the camp moved out, all armed with spears.

‚Äî Another victory for Eldia. ‚Äî Heinrich said.

‚Äî As usual. It's good that I won't have to worry about damage when I fight like my uncle in the future.

‚Äî Yes, I've heard that previous Jaw Titans were damaged by trebuchet stones. I bet it was simply because of the user's neglect, the Jaw could have easily dodged the projectiles.

As Heinrich talked, S√∂ren's mind thought about other things. His lifespan would be cut short to thirteen more years, he would have to kill without hesitation, his responsibilities would be even greater‚Ä¶ If only there was another eligible heir of age. Strangely, the Brandt clan was composed by many children and many elders, and the few adults abstained from inheriting the Armoured.

Heinrich waved his hand over S√∂ren's eyes.

‚Äî Are you listening to me?

He stared blankly at Heinrich.

‚Äî Have you ever stopped to think that we'll die early? That we'll kill hundreds of thousands?

‚Äî Erm‚Ä¶ Yes, but why bring it up now? ‚Äî Heinrich scratched his own head.

‚Äî Doesn't that upset you?

‚Äî Why? We're doing this for the glory of Eldia! It is as our ancestors wanted. Besides, these other people are inferior to us. Blessed are the subjects of Ymir who can channel part of her power!

S√∂ren decided not to talk anymore. His fate was already decided. Liking it or not, he would inherit the Armoured Titan. The other Eldians in the war camp cheered as Klaus came back, still in titan form. The non-Eldian auxiliaries stood silent, trembling in fear.

‚Äî You see that, boy?

S√∂ren turned around to look at the middle-aged man who spoke to him. It was Alexamenos, that despite not being an Eldian, was a high-ranking officer. He apparently was the advisor of a king and tricked the entire court, in the end leading to the Eldian army "peacefully" conquering the kingdom. His greying hair was short, and a stubble covered his lower face.

‚Äî You will inherit this power. By Ymir, I wish I was an Eldian like you! ‚Äî Alexamenos said enthusiastically.

name:
Poetry and prose professions
The editorial staff receives many letters every day. These letters are sincere and frank. One can feel that their authors want to confess and ask for advice. After all, it's easier to tell a stranger everything about yourself, even the most intimate, most cherished things, than it is to your closest friend.
These two letters came at the same time. Both were from girls of the same age. One girl, after graduating from high school, went to work in an office, and she is depressed by the monotony of her simple, but mundane work. She envies those who are always on the road, who sleep in tents, who see the starry sky above them instead of the ceiling.
Another girl became a surveyor. She spends weeks or even months in the field, which is why she misses the bustling city so much, and envies her peers who can go to discos every night, if not to museums and theaters, then at least to discos. She hates her profession. "I think I'm on the wrong train. I should change trains, but it's so hard to do that now," she writes.
Indeed, it is difficult now. Just as it is not easy, after all, to choose the right train on time and correctly. 
What a false and sham idea our young people have about different professions! For them, a doctor is a face in a gauze bandage, a bright lamp over a surgical table. Relatives are waiting at the door of the operating room, already with flowers, because they are convinced that the operation will go well. For young people, a steelmaker is a hard look, a determined expression on a man's face, a bright flame of the open-hearth furnace... A geologist is a backpack, edelweiss, waterfalls, risky but always successful crossings of stormy mountain rivers, a guitar by a picturesque campfire... 
How easy it is to portray the external attributes of professions! And how difficult it is to reveal the true essence of the profession! Here you have to understand the prose of people's daily hard work, because without prose there is no poetry.
The life of a geologist is months, if not years, of processing collected materials. It is off-road, unsettled, often homeless and familyless. In addition to the beauty of mountain gorges and the exoticism of dense thickets, it is fierce mosquitoes and annoying fly flies, and endless fatigue.
The life of a surgeon is a continuous physical and mental strain, healing human wounds and ulcers. It is a daily routine of receiving suffering and sometimes irritated patients, exhausting night shifts.  Often, it is also the most difficult moral duty to tell the family that despite all efforts, it was not possible to save the patient...
A teacher's life is not just armfuls of flowers on exam day. It's piles of notebooks that have to be checked until late at night, noise in the classroom, jostling during breaks, forty students with different, difficult personalities... And there are forty in each class, but how many in total? And in a lifetime?
So look closely at the people, at their work, at the prose and poetry of the professions that interest you! So that you don't have to change trains later.

Suppose I am conducting a research paper on time series data entitled ‚ÄúThe Nexus Among Oil Price, Stock Market, and Exchange Rate During Recent Pandemic & Russia-Ukraine Crisis: Fresh Evidence from UK Economy‚Äù. Here I have taken three variables Stock Index (SI), Brent Oil Price (OP), and Exchange Rate (ER). I have taken time series data from 2014-2023 segmenting into four periods. 2014-2019 for Pre-covid Period; 2020-2021 for Covid Period; 2022-2023 for War Period and 2014-2023 for the Overall Period. My Research Questions are:
1. Does each variable have a direct influence on others?
2. Does each variable granger cause one another and does the stock market work as a mediating variable for shock transmission?
3. Is there any moderating impact of oil price on the dynamic conditional correlation (DCC) between the stock market and exchange rate?

For data analysis, I have checked other relevant literature.

For research question 1, most of them used the VAR model to check the direct influence of variables on each other. For research question 2, most of them used VAR Granger Causality and determined if the stock market transmits the shock as a mediating variable or not. I haven‚Äôt found any paper on my 3rd research question but a paper suggested a technique to address it in their future research question. I am giving their exact quotation, ‚ÄúThe moderating effect of oil can be estimated by using the NARDL framework for studying the direct influence of OP on the DCCs between SI and ER‚Äù.

But the problem is that, for my 1st and 2nd, I can‚Äôt use the VAR model as I have autocorrelation and heteroskedasticity which I can‚Äôt remove even after log transforming or log differencing the variable. I also can‚Äôt use VECM Model either as my variables are not co-integrated from the Johansen co-integration test. Therefore give me a solution for my model. Which other econometric model can I use that takes autocorrelation and heteroskedasticity into account for my 1st and 2nd research questions as well as also give me guidelines on how to approach the analysis of my 3rd research question? I am really lost here. I don‚Äôt know how to analyze the process in R. And What about VAR-DCC-GARCH, I have seen some research paper used it. Does it suit my research question? research objectives:  
1. to study the concept of "scientific text" in linguistic research, to consider its characteristics, the peculiarities of translation.
2. to study the concept of "philosophical text" in linguistic research, considering its characteristics, features.
3. To consider specific strategies and techniques in the translation of scientific texts of philosophical orientation.
4. Conduct pre-translation analysis of Popper's philosophical texts, identifying potential difficulties of translation.
5. Analyze strategies and techniques of translation of philosophical texts in the works of K. Popper


result.
We have considered various definitions for the concept of a scientific text and for our work we settled on Eugene Naida's definition.
We considered the problem of identifying philosophical texts, but taking Patrick Blackburn's definition as the basis, we identified philosophical texts as a subspecies of scientific texts.

We have identified the following problems in the translation of philosophical texts
1. Conceptual and terminological variation:
2. Ambiguity and polysemy:
3. multi-level argumentation and dialectic:
4 . Cultural and historical specificity:
5. Intertextuality
To address them, identified the following strategies
1. Dynamic equivalence and formal equivalence
2. Scopus theory and communicative orientation approach
3. typology of text and language in translation
And the following techniques
1. transliteration as a specific translation technique (direct translation
2. Modulation as a polysemic approach (indirect translation)
3. Translation commentary as a way of explaining translation (indirect translation)
4. Neologism as a translation solution (indirect translation)

A pre-translation analysis of Popper's ideas and theories revealed potential difficulties in translation: conceptual and terminological variation; ambiguity and polysemy; difficulty in maintaining authorial argumentation and logical coherence; cultural and historical specificity; intertextuality. An analysis of existing translations of Popper's texts highlighted examples of problems and inconsistencies in translations of key terms and concepts.
Based on the analysis of the translation of 30 fragments of scientific text of philosophical orientation, it was found that the most commonly used approach is modulation, 15 fragments were translated using this method. Modulation was the second most common approach, used for 10 fragments to solve the translation problem. The translator turned to creating neologisms only 5 times. And the translation commentary as a translation solution when translating a philosophical text was additionally used as a secondary technique throughout the translation.
In conclusion, the translator of philosophical texts should have a background knowledge of philosophy, covering not only the work of the translated author, but also the whole philosophy and cultural specificity in the intertextuality of the translated text. The translator must be aware of the potential problems in translating philosophical texts and be able to find an approach to them, based on the strategies and techniques suggested by various scholars.

Give a suitable, alluring and jargon and compact sub-heading in five six words                             While it may be tempting to believe that we are living in an era of globalization, characterised by rapid technological advancements, intensified cross-cultural exchanges, and the proliferation of knowledge systems, contemporary societies are still deeply rooted in Eurocentric frameworks of thinking. The long-lasting impact of colonialism, imperialism, and global power asymmetries continue to shape the cognitive, cultural, and social domains of academia, politics, and media. These influences propagate various orientalist stereotypes, oppressive binaries, and discriminatory practices that impede the development of a genuinely pluralistic and egalitarian world. Eurocentrism can be defined as an epistemological framework that situates European culture, history, and values as the defining center of the world, while at the same time disregarding or belittling the contributions of other cultures and civilisations. This ethnocentric positioning perceives the Europe or West as a paragon of universal values and cultural superiority, leading to a systematic undervaluation and misrepresentation of non-European cultures. Central to the Eurocentric paradigm is the construction of a dichotomy between the West and the so-called ‚Äúnon-West,‚Äù which is characterized by essentialist and often discriminatory distinctions between these two spheres. As noted by Edward Said (1979), this binary opposition manifests itself in various forms of discourse, such as history, literature, music and art, where non-European societies are stereotypically depicted as exotic, inferior, irrational, fanatic and backward in comparison to the civilised, rational, and progressive European model. European culture, according to him ‚Äúgained strength and identity by setting itself off against the Orient as a sort of surrogate and even underground self.‚Äù (3) In other words, the Orient functions as a mirror to the West in that the West relies heavily on its counterpart, the Orient, for its own sense of superiority. (Sandy and Ouardi, 2019, p. 129) This paradigm, therefore, not only consolidates the stature of the West, but also perpetuates the subordination of non-European societies within global power structures, and the spheres of knowledge and influence. Said‚Äôs work on Orientalism provides a seminal critique of this discourse, demonstrating how its utilization has justified colonization, exploitation, and violence against Eastern civilizations.
	The Knowledge production or the representation of the Orient in Western narratives is not a recent development; it has existed since the earliest times. Edward Said traces the development of these knowledge-producing mechanisms, which Foucault referred to as ‚Äúregimes of truths,‚Äù as far back as ancient Greece, with particular reference to two plays by Aeschylus. The early portrayals of the Orient as a ‚Äúhostile other,‚Äù ‚Äúa world beyond the seas‚Äù have evolved and expanded alongside colonial endeavours, with literary works often serving as propaganda tools to spread false images of the colonized territories. As Said writes, 
The ‚ÄúOrient was created -or, as I call it, ‚ÄúOrientalized‚Äù- and to believe that such things happen simply as a necessity of the imagination is to be disingenuous‚Ä¶ The Orient was Orientalized not only because it was discovered to be ‚ÄúOriental‚Äù in all those ways considered commonplace by an average nineteenth-century European, but also because it could be -that is, submitted to being- made Oriental.‚Äù (5-6)
Said also highlights the power imbalance between the West and the Orient as a critical factor in shaping these universalized images, which reinforce Western dominance. Essentially, the Orientalist discourse is contingent upon a distinct power dynamic that enables the West to create and maintain reductive images of the East. Exercising control over the Orient‚Äôs representation, the West situates itself as the observer, imbued with the power to discipline by defining what the East is and is not. The ‚Äúpower/knowledge‚Äù nexus ‚Äì the notion that the production, dissemination, and control of knowledge serve as primary agents of power is reminiscent of the Panopticon, wherein the West becomes the observer, the bearer of the power-laden gaze, determining the Eastern identity, norms, morals and interests. This gaze reifies a grid of intelligibility that legitimates specific research as objective knowledge. Nevertheless, existing critiques of Orientalism seldom address the central role of gender in the construction of these discourses. As a consequence, the ways in which the gendered identities of colonised women have been manipulated to serve Western imperialist interests remain underexplored. As Ann Laura Stoler notes in her work Carnal Knowledge and Imperial Power (2010), gender is often used as a tool for controlling and regulating colonised populations. Therefore, in response, this paper aims to extend Said‚Äôs analytical framework to incorporate the nexus between gender and imperialism, exploring how the Western discursive configuration of colonized women has reinforced and justified modes of subjugation and control.

Sentiment Analysis in Retail and Social Media

The continuous growth and expansion of the online retail industry have led to a massive emergence of user-generated content, especially in the form of customer reviews and opinions, which hold valuable information for both consumers and companies (Wu & Chang, 2020). Understanding customer sentiment has become a critical factor in driving customer satisfaction and shaping marketing strategies in retail (Ahmed, Agarwal, Kurniawan, Anantadjaya, & Krishnan, 2022). This literature review explores the concept of sentiment analysis, its application in the retail sector, and the role of social media, machine learning, and natural language processing in this research area.

Sentiment Analysis

Sentiment analysis refers to the process of extracting and analyzing emotions expressed in text, providing an understanding of the user‚Äôs attitude or sentiment towards a particular topic, product, service, or entity (Han & Moghaddam, 2021; Agrawal & Mittal, 2022). It typically involves categorizing opinions into positive, negative, and neutral classes (Dadhich & Thankachan, 2022) and can be employed in various fields, including politics, elections, movies, retail businesses, and microblogs (Aziz & Dimililer, 2020).

Text Analysis

Text analysis is an essential component of sentiment analysis, as it deals with the extraction of meaningful information from text data through various techniques such as natural language processing, text mining, and machine learning (Braga, Brito, & Roxo, 2022; Nithuna & Laseena, 2022). It helps in understanding customer reviews, identifying the key topics, and deriving insights that can be used for decision-making and strategy formulation in retail (Pettersson, Oucheikh, & Lofstrom, 2022).

Twitter Analysis

Twitter has become a popular platform for users to express their opinions and sentiments on various topics, including retail products and services (Dastidar, Shivakumar, Viswanathan, & Suresh, 2021; Cirqueira et al., 2020). As a result, Twitter analysis has emerged as a crucial area of sentiment analysis, focusing on extracting and processing tweets to gauge customer sentiment and predict market trends (Tran, Pallant, & Johnson, 2021; Ahmed, ElKorany, & ElSayed, 2022).

Retail

The retail sector has embraced sentiment analysis to gain insights into customer preferences, needs, and emotional responses to products and services in order to improve customer satisfaction and competitiveness (Dutta, Maitra, Ghosh, Chatterjee, Goto, & Sen, 2022; Lappeman, Clark, Evans, & Sierra-Rubia, 2020). Moreover, online retail platforms such as Amazon and Flipkart generate extensive textual data in the form of user reviews, making sentiment analysis a valuable tool for retailers to adapt their marketing strategies and enhance customer experiences (Han & Moghaddam, 2021; Mokadam, Shivakumar, Viswanathan, & Suresh, 2021).

Sentiment Analysis in Social Media

Social media platforms have become a critical source of customer feedback and opinions, with customers increasingly discussing their experiences and sentiments towards retail products and services (Budianto, Wirjodirdjo, Maflahah, & Kurnianingtyas, 2022; Loke & Steentjes, 2022). Sentiment analysis in social media helps retailers monitor customer opinions, identify trends, and track critical issues (Dadhich & Thankachan, 2022). It also allows companies to understand how customers perceive their brand, enabling them to make informed decisions and develop targeted marketing campaigns (Budianto et al., 2022).

Machine Learning

Machine learning techniques play a crucial role in sentiment analysis, as they enable the development of models capable of automatically identifying and categorizing sentiments in text data (Dastidar et al., 2021; Dutta et al., 2022). Various machine learning algorithms, such as Na√Øve Bayes, Logistic Regression, Stochastic Gradient Descent, Random Forest, Decision Tree, and Support Vector Machine, have been used to build sentiment analysis models, with ensemble methods such as weighted majority voting or stacking demonstrating improved performance compared to individual classifiers (Aziz & Dimililer, 2020; Nithuna & Laseena, 2022).

Natural Language Processing

Natural Language Processing (NLP) is another critical component of sentiment analysis, as it deals with the automatic analysis and understanding of human language in textual form (Ahmed et al., 2022). NLP techniques are utilized to process, clean, and analyze text data in order to conduct sentiment analysis and extract meaningful insights (Pettersson et al., 2022; Harn Y, & Moghaddam M, 2021). Moreover, advancements in deep learning and NLP, such as the development of the BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers) language model, have significantly improved the performance of sentiment analysis methods (Han & Moghaddam, 2021).
